subtopic: Managing time in a heavy semester
passage: The power went out at seven on Sunday evening, so Kiran and Saurabh sat with a phone torch and the paper planner. This was the weekly check. Kiran read the week aloud: two lab reports done, the statistics revision half done, the gym missed twice. "Why did the revision slip?" Saurabh asked. "Because I put it after the club meeting and I was tired." That was the signal. The unfinished revision moved to a morning slot next week. With only the torch battery to spare, Kiran also crossed out the second club meeting, since the week was already too full. The paper looked lighter. Saurabh took a photo for the shared list.

qa.q: At what time did the power go out on Sunday?
qa.a: The power went out at seven on Sunday evening.

qa.q: What did Kiran realise about why the revision slipped?
qa.a: Kiran realised that the revision had been put after the club meeting when Kiran was tired, so it needed a morning slot.

qa.q: What other approach could work if the plan is too full again next week?
qa.a: Kiran could pick the one commitment that matters least each Sunday and drop it early, since a lighter week is easier to keep.

qa.q: How might Saurabh see the weekly check?
qa.a: Saurabh probably finds it useful and calming, since the questions helped Kiran see the reason instead of just feeling guilty.

grounding: Each Sunday a student checks what was done and what slipped, moves unfinished items to next week and cuts a commitment when it is too full.

subtopic: Managing time in a heavy semester
passage:
Every Sunday at five, Arnab sat on the terrace of his PG in Bengaluru with his planner and a cup of filter coffee and did what his senior Asif had taught him: the review.
Three questions. What did I finish? What slipped? Why?
This Sunday: finished the database assignment and two lab records. Slipped: the reading for Monday's seminar, and the gym on Thursday. Why? The coding club meeting on Wednesday had run three hours instead of one, and he'd said yes to helping with their event too.
He moved the seminar reading into Monday morning's first slot and the gym into Tuesday. Then he looked at the coming week: two tests, a presentation, the club event. Too full. He messaged the club lead that he could help at the event but not with the planning meetings.
Asif, passing with laundry, glanced at the planner. 'You cut something. Good.'

qa.q: What three questions did Arnab ask in the review?
qa.a: What did I finish? What slipped? Why?

qa.q: How might Arnab have felt looking at the coming week?
qa.a: He likely felt a bit overwhelmed seeing two tests, a presentation and an event, which pushed him to cut the planning meetings.

qa.q: What else could Arnab add to the Sunday review?
qa.a: A note of any task that slips two weeks running, so he can decide whether to drop it or change how he does it.

qa.q: How does Asif see the planner?
qa.a: Asif approves, seeing that Arnab has learned to cut something when the week is too full.

grounding: Shows a student reviewing each Sunday what was done and what slipped, moving unfinished items into the next week and cutting a commitment when it is too full.

subtopic: Managing time in a heavy semester
passage:
'Sunday review time,' Charu said, dropping onto Vasudha's bed. 'Show me.'
Vasudha opened her planner. 'Done: stats assignment, two chapters of sociology, laundry. Slipped: the literature essay draft and my Wednesday swim.'
'Why?'
'The essay... I kept starting it at eleven at night. And swimming, I skipped because I'd stayed up for the essay I didn't write.'
Charu laughed. 'So one problem ate two things.'
'Exactly.' Vasudha moved the essay into Monday and Tuesday mornings, two hours each. 'Mornings. Not nights.' Then she looked at the week ahead and frowned. 'Tests on Wednesday and Friday, essay due Friday, and I promised to help at the book drive on Thursday.'
'That's a lot.'
'It's too much. I'll ask Meghna to swap Thursday with me for next week.' She typed the message and hit send. 'There. Done.'

qa.q: Which two things slipped last week?
qa.a: The literature essay draft and the Wednesday swim.

qa.q: How does Vasudha seem to feel after sending the message to Meghna?
qa.a: Vasudha seems relieved and in control, having turned an overfull week into one that fits.

qa.q: What else could Vasudha try if the morning essay slots also slip?
qa.a: Break the essay into one small part per slot, like an outline on Monday, so starting feels easier.

qa.q: How does the Sunday review look to Charu?
qa.a: Charu treats it as a friendly ritual and helps by asking 'why', spotting that one problem ate two things.

grounding: Shows a student reviewing on Sunday what was done, what slipped and why, moving the unfinished essay into next week and swapping out one commitment.
